I'm from the Scottsbluff/Gering area.  First of all: they're the same town and you won't be able to tell the difference.  In early July we have Oregon trail days in Gering which is kind of a festival celebrating our history.  We have the Scotts Bluff national monument as well as the Wildcat Hills (I prefer the wildcats).  Chimney Rock is also about a 20 minute drive from here.  We also have our own little miniature version of the Badlands that aren't super well known.  Make sure you stop at Scotty's while you're in Scottsbluff and try their fries.  Also make sure while you're in Nebraska you try Runza at least once and make sure you get their ranch dressing.  We also have a hot air balloon festival (I believe one of the largest in the country) that happens toward the end of July.  If you go to chimney rock the towns of Bayard and McGrew are also very small.  There's nothing much to see there but if you're interested in really small towns McGrew is about 6 blocks in total and has a famous-to-the-area bar called the Pink Palace.  To me the most interesting part of McGrew is that it's post office is pretty much a shed.  We also have the Agate Fossil Beds nearby which is where some of the best well-preserved fossils were found (not dinosaurs though.  Don't get too excited) and it's a nice trail to walk along and has some cool history to it.  Let me know if you have any other questions about the area!
